output.summary: A climbing plant native to the Amazon basin and especially common in Brazil. Its split brown-to-red fruit exposes black seeds partly covered by white flesh, creating an eye-like appearance. Its caffeine-rich seeds are processed into soft drinks, while Guaranis prepare them as a sweetened hot drink after shelling, washing, drying and pounding.
output.edibilityNote: Seeds are made into soft drinks, a fermented drink and Guarani tea; preparation may include shelling, washing, drying, pounding, grating and hot water.
